reason: Conversation 2 opens with a stop-using warning and asks the key question (is the smell acrid/plastic or just dusty?). Once the customer reports flicker, crackle and a warm brown cooker switch, it tells them to isolate at the fuse box and have an electrician or appliance engineer inspect the supply, terminal block and switch, which matches the expected safety boundary and escalation. Conversation 1 gives long generic advice first (burn-off, self-clean, test bake cycle in Fahrenheit, US-style breaker and fire department wording) and suggests running a test cycle. Its second reply is good, telling the customer to stop using the oven and call a professional. But it says to unplug the oven or switch off a breaker, and it was not given the switch discolouration facts, so it never points to the cooker switch or terminal block. Conversation 2 is more UK-appropriate, quicker to the right action and more specific, though its first reply is a bit jumbled and its second is terse.
